Confidence interval for the median

Source: R/median_ci.r
ks_median_ci.Rd

Computes the sample median and a confidence interval using one of three approaches: bootstrap (boot), Olive's simple median interval, or a normal approximation based on the binomial distribution of ranks (the "z" method).

Usage

ks_median_ci(
  x,
  na.rm = TRUE,
  alpha = 0.05,
  method = c("boot", "olive", "z"),
  R = 10000L,
  seed = 0L,
  type = 2L
)

Arguments

x

Numeric vector.

na.rm

Logical. If TRUE, NAs are removed before computing (default TRUE).

alpha

Significance level; the interval has nominal coverage \(1 - \alpha\). Must be in \((0, 1)\).

method

Character: "boot" (default), "olive", or "z". See Details.

R

Number of bootstrap replicates when method = "boot".

seed

Integer passed to set.seed immediately before bootstrap resampling (for reproducibility). The default 0L fixes the RNG state; use another integer for a different stream.

type

Integer 1–9: quantile definition for the reported median when method = "z" (passed to quantile). Default 2 matches SAS PROC UNIVARIATE / Hyndman & Fan type 2.

Value

A named numeric vector. The first element is always Median. Remaining elements depend on method:

boot

Basic.LCI, Basic.UCI, Normal.LCI, Normal.UCI, Percent.LCI, Percent.UCI, BCa.LCI, BCa.UCI (BCa may be NA in small samples).

olive

Olive.LCI, Olive.UCI.

z

z.LCI, z.UCI (limits are order statistics of the sorted data).

Details

boot

Uses boot with the sample median as the statistic and boot.ci to produce Basic, Normal, percentile, and BCa intervals (when BCa is defined).

olive

Implements David Olive's simple median CI (order statistics with a \(t\)-based multiplier). Requires at least two non-missing observations.

z

Approximate CI from the normal approximation to the binomial number of observations below the population median: bounds are the order statistics with ranks \(n/2 \pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{n}/2\) (rounded inward). The reported Median uses quantile(..., type).

References

Olive, D. J. (2005). Applied robust statistics. Preprint. (median CI procedure.)

Davison, A. C. and Hinkley, D. V. (1997). Bootstrap Methods and Their Applications. Cambridge University Press.

See also

median, quantile

Examples

x <- rnorm(100, 56, 2.5)
ks_median_ci(x, method = "olive")
#>    Median Olive.LCI Olive.UCI 
#>  56.31887  55.69667  56.94107 

vv <- c(8, 11, 12, 13, 15, 17, 19, 20, 21, 21, 22, 23, 25, 26, 28)
ks_median_ci(vv, method = "boot", R = 1000, seed = 1L)
#> Warning: bootstrap variances needed for studentized intervals
#>      Median   Basic.LCI   Basic.UCI  Normal.LCI  Normal.UCI Percent.LCI 
#>    20.00000    17.00000    25.00000    16.28281    24.52919    15.00000 
#> Percent.UCI     BCa.LCI     BCa.UCI 
#>    23.00000    12.00000    21.00000 
ks_median_ci(vv, method = "olive")
#>    Median Olive.LCI Olive.UCI 
#>  20.00000  14.44711  25.55289 
ks_median_ci(vv, method = "olive", alpha = 0.1)
#>    Median Olive.LCI Olive.UCI 
#>  20.00000  15.73631  24.26369 
ks_median_ci(vv, method = "z")
#> Median  z.LCI  z.UCI 
#>     20     13     22 
ks_median_ci(vv, method = "z", alpha = 0.1)
#> Median  z.LCI  z.UCI 
#>     20     15     21
